deep_dive.title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
deep_dive.abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Evaluating the third ability requires reliably executing an experiment that an agent designs, with readings grounded in a real laboratory. We introduce TwinLab-Bench, which evaluates AI scientists on self-designed experiments in 52 tasks from laboratories in the physical sciences, the life sciences, and engineering. The benchmark supports more than 100 experimental action types, and the agent's report is scored by comparison with a hidden answer taken from real laboratory records. Each task has its own TwinLab agent, an agent that serves as the environment and executes the experiments that the tested agent designs, reading the raw materials of the laboratory and calling calculators that are built from its records. Compared with a language model that sees only the task description, the TwinLab agent almost eliminates readings that deviate from the real records and inconsistent answers to a repeated request, and closed-book probes control for answers recalled from memory. We find that these tasks remain hard for frontier models: the strongest, Claude Fable 5.2, averages a score of only 45.0, and we conduct an empirical study of where it fails.

quick_skim.title: RAVEN: A Self-RAG Based Agent for Threat Classification and Response
quick_skim.abstract: Security event analysis in large enterprises can be overwhelming, as each alert typically requires manual in- spection by human operators. This process is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies, especially in high-volume Secu- rity Operations Center (SOC) environments. In this work- in-progress paper, we present RAVEN: Retrieval-Augmented Vulnerability & Event aNalysis, an agentic framework designed to support SOC analysts by automating the initial stages of alert investigation. The proposed system leverages a Self- Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation-based approach to provide an initial classification of security events and enables interactive refinement through analyst-in-the-loop queries. Un- like traditional approaches that rely on generic mitigation strategies, RAVEN generates context-aware remediation sug- gestions by incorporating knowledge of the target enterprise infrastructure. We implement an early-stage prototype and report preliminary results on three balanced test sets of 400 curated web payloads each (SQLi, XSS, SSTI) and a qualitative case study of mitigation generation; an evaluation on IDS- generated alerts and a user study are ongoing and outlined as remaining work.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: SOC analysts face overwhelming alert volumes. RAVEN is a self-reflective retrieval-augmented generation agent that classifies security events and supports analyst-in-the-loop refinement, automating early alert triage.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 大型企业中安全告警数量巨大，人工逐条排查耗时且易出现不一致，安全运营中心亟需自动化初筛手段。作者提出RAVEN，一个基于自反思检索增强生成的智能体框架，先对安全事件做初步分类，再通过分析师在环查询进行交互式修正。该工作为进行中的研究，展示了将检索增强生成与智能体流程结合用于告警调查的可行路径。其贡献在于把RAG式知识检索引入安全运维场景，减轻分析师的重复劳动并提升处置一致性。
